mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 6% triggers a recessionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered instances, or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coinciding with a rise in the housing market (HOUST > 1.5% MoM), indicates a supply-side shock that reduces corporate earnings and increases inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for three consecutive months AND HOUST > 1.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive easing cycle that boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals improving consumer purchasing power, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the median return is zero or negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in unemployment rate to below 3.5% while payrolls growth (PAYEMS) accelerates above 0.7% MoM for two months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and prompts preemptive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 0.7% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces household wealth and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is positive.
